key_insight: UNSM-treated Cr₃C₂–NiCr coatings showed sample-dependent hardness, with different treatment settings producing the highest values for DS and HVOF deposits.
engineering_relevance: Selecting UNSM settings for sprayed coatings requires assessing local hardness alongside surface integrity rather than assuming uniform improvement.
method: Evaluated four UNSM-treated samples per deposition route: detonation spray (DS) and high-velocity oxy-fuel (HVOF).
Used static loads of 20 or 30 N and vibration amplitudes of 20 or 30 µm.
Measured instrumental hardness at 300 mN with a 10 s dwell and examined post-scratch surfaces by SEM.
evidence_signal: Hardness ranged from 820–970 HV for DS and 546–1165 HV for HVOF, peaking at DS-T1 (20 N/20 µm) and HVOF-T4 (30 N/30 µm), respectively.
watch_item: Post-scratch SEM observations do not isolate UNSM-induced damage or establish a scratch-resistance ranking.
paper_title: HARDNESS AND POST-SCRATCH SURFACE MORPHOLOGY OF Cr₃C₂–NiCr COATINGS AFTER ULTRASONIC NANOCRYSTAL SURFACE MODIFICATION
